- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., 79.16 → 82.41 or 79.23 → 82.23), then corrects with a downward bias later.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too high a mean, fails to adjust downward when prices show signs of cooling.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the 10–20 day window, then gradually converge toward true values — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term volatility.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 20–30 day horizon, especially when history shows consolidation or downward momentum.
- When history includes a recent spike, model often overreacts with a peak forecast, then undercorrects — creating a “peak-pool” pattern.
- Model fails to account for downward momentum in the last 5–7 days of history — often underestimates the drop or ignores it entirely.
- Forecasts are more accurate when history shows a clear downward trend — model underperforms when history is flat or mildly upward.
